title: Theo and the Portrait
premise: Emrys Thackeray hosts a late-night call-in show, and one October week the callers are all people who died days ago — including her own sister. When she investigates the source to a decaying house where a family portrait repaints itself nightly, she discovers the portrait is counting down its subjects: whoever it finishes first is claimed. Emrys, a skeptic forced into belief, moves in as the live-in 'caretaker' to protect the household — a widowed father, his two children, and their aunt — while wrestling with her growing love for the father and her duty to the dead. The final count comes down to Emrys herself: she offers her face to the canvas in exchange for the family's release, but the youngest child's act of found-family love smears the paint mid-stroke, trapping the hungry painter inside his own portrait forever.
about_author: E. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent years answering calls from strangers at 3 a.m. and never quite shook the feeling that some of them weren't among the living. They write horror about grief, small towns, and the terrible intimacy of voices in the dark.

chapters.title: The Dead Line
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. During her midnight radio shift, a caller describes her own funeral from last Tuesday; then a second dead caller asks for Emrys by name. She laughs it off on air, but her hands shake through the sign-off. Emotional beat: denial cracking under the first impossible voice.

chapters.title: Sister Static
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The next night, her estranged sister Wren calls the show — three days after drowning. Wren says only: 'It's counting us, Emmy. Don't let it finish.' The line goes dead; so does the station transmitter. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into dread.

chapters.title: Hollowell House
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Tracing the calls' origin, Emrys drives to Hollowell House, a shuttered estate where a family died in 1911 — except records say they didn't. A current family lives there now, and every mirror inside reflects one second late. Emotional beat: skeptic's curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Family That Answers
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She meets the Aldridges: widowed father Silas, teens Mara and Theo, and Aunt Cordelia, who pretends the mirrors are 'old glass.' Emrys notices fresh flowers arranged for someone no one names. Emotional beat: warmth offered by people hiding something.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The boy's perspective: he's known about the lag since his mother died; the mirror shows her sometimes, standing where you were a heartbeat ago. He watches the new caretaker arrive and hopes she'll see what he sees. Emotional beat: lonely child's guarded hope.

chapters.title: The Portrait Repaints
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the gallery hangs an unfinished 1911 portrait of five figures; by morning, a sixth figure has appeared — wearing Wren's drowned face. Cordelia burns the canvas; by dusk it's whole again, and the sixth figure has hands now. Emotional beat: horror made intimate and personal.

chapters.title: Rules of the Count
chapters.summary: POV Cordelia. The aunt's history: her grandmother survived the first count by leaving before the portrait finished; the painting claims whoever it completes first, and it always finishes someone. Cordelia has kept the family alive for thirty years by keeping them moving. Emotional beat: exhausted duty, love expressed as vigilance.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The daughter tests the mirror deliberately, trading secrets with her mother's reflection for clues about the count. The reflection gives one true answer: 'The painter needs a face that consents.' Emotional beat: teenage recklessness masking heartbreak.

chapters.title: Hired Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys takes the live-in caretaker position officially, telling herself it's research for a broadcast exposé. Her first night alone in the east wing, the radio in her room turns itself on — playing her own show, from tomorrow. Emotional beat: complicity; she's moved in and can't pretend otherwise.

chapters.title: Silas
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A quiet chapter: Silas and Emrys repair the greenhouse together, and he admits he heard his late wife's voice on the radio the night before he almost walked into the lake. They agree, wordlessly, to keep each other here. Emotional beat: two grieving people choosing each other's company.

chapters.title: The Fifth Figure
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The portrait's original five figures begin moving between viewings — turning heads, shifting hands. Theo realizes the fifth figure isn't a 1911 ancestor anymore; it's becoming his mother, and she looks tired of waiting. Emotional beat: a child recognizing his parent's ghost as something no longer safe.

chapters.title: Broadcast From the House
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys smuggles in recording gear and does a secret episode from the gallery, interviewing the family about the count. Playback reveals a seventh voice beneath theirs, patiently reciting names — the list of everyone the portrait has finished. Emotional beat: evidence that should vindicate her instead terrifies her.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Cordelia. Flashback-chapter: in 1994, Cordelia offered the portrait her own face to save her brother's family; it refused her — too willing. Consent freely given is the only currency it takes, and desperation doesn't count. Emotional beat: guilt over decades of half-measures.

chapters.title: Mara Runs
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Convinced distance means safety, Mara flees to a friend's house in town — and finds the friend's bathroom mirror already running a second behind, showing Mara's face completing stroke by stroke. Distance doesn't matter once you're counted. Emotional beat: the collapse of the escape plan.

chapters.title: The Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At 3 a.m., the house radio broadcasts tomorrow's show early: the dead caller reads tonight's date and one name — Theo's. The portrait's sixth figure now has a complete face, and it isn't Wren's anymore. Emotional beat: deadline made explicit; panic becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Unfinished Business
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Researching the 1911 painter, Edmund Hollowell, Emrys learns he died mid-self-portrait, and the family portrait was his last work — a trap he built to finish himself through others. The only way to end a count is to give the painter a face he can't refuse. Emotional beat: the plan forming, and what it will cost.

chapters.title: Consent
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys tells Silas the truth and her plan: she'll sit for the portrait willingly, offering a consenting face to bind Hollowell inside his own unfinished self-portrait. Silas refuses; they fight; she leaves the letter explaining anyway. Emotional beat: love against duty, both refusing to yield.

chapters.title: The Sitting
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Midnight. Emrys sits before the portrait and gives consent aloud; the paint begins climbing her arms like cold water, and the sixth figure dissolves to make room. Across the house, every mirror shows her image finishing without her. Emotional beat: sacrificial calm over screaming instinct.

chapters.title: Theo's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo breaks the rules — runs into the gallery, grabs the brush, and paints himself into the frame beside her, declaring the family incomplete unless it includes all of them. The portrait, built to take one, cannot resolve two claims at once; the strokes stutter. Emotional beat: found family as literal interference.

chapters.title: The Smear
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Inside the painting's pull, Emrys hears Wren's voice one last time — not a lure this time, but a goodbye — and uses the stolen second of stillness to drag her palm across the wet canvas, smearing Hollowell's emerging face into ruin. The house screams through every mirror at once. Emotional beat: defiance at the point of no return.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Dawn. The portrait is a blank, ruined canvas; the mirrors run on time; the radio plays static and nothing else. Cordelia weeps over thirty years of vigilance suddenly unnecessary. Silas finds Emrys alive on the gallery floor, paint-burned but breathing, holding Theo's hand. Emotional beat: survival disbelieved, then believed.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Weeks later, Emrys returns to the airwaves from a rebuilt studio in Hollowell House, the family around her as she ends her final broadcast: 'To everyone who called — thank you. You can rest now.' One last caller breathes thanks and hangs up forever. Emotional beat: peace earned, grief honored, family chosen.
